newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WOOLTRU UNIT BUYS DEBTORS BOOK FROM STANBIC.
newsitem.headline: WOOLTRU UNIT BUYS DEBTORS BOOK FROM STANBIC.

text.p: South Africa's Woolworths said on Thursday it will take over the funding of its private label credit card from Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd (Stanbic) in a move which will see the retailer absorb an 850 million rand debtors book.

Ian Sturrock, the financial director of Woolworths, which is a subsidiary of the listed Wooltru Ltd group said in a statement that the July 1 purchase will easily be absorbed due to the group's cash generating ability.
"Our financial statements for the year to June 30 will reflect the debtors' book on balance sheet and gearing will remain within acceptable norms," Sturrock said.
Stanbic has funded the card since its inception in 1993.

Woolworths said that over the four years it had gained signficant experience in managing the private label card scheme, over which it had marketing and administrative control, and had recently accepted responsibility for some of the credit risk.
"The decision to take on the funding of the card is a logical progression towards total independence in the operation of the scheme," it said.

Sturrock said that Woolworths had over one million approved accounts and although cash sales remained the core of its business, credit sales generated over 30 percent, or about four billion rand, in annual sales.
Noel Webb, Stanbic's managing director of retail banking said that the transfer of the book would not have a negative impact on the bank's income statement due to the adequacey of its provision.
Stanbic will continue to provide Woolworths with banking and other financial services.
